# OpenCode Unlimited

**Single local OpenAI / Anthropic-compatible gateway** that combines the strongest ideas from the major community “unlimited” repos for OpenCode Zen free models.

| Source repo | What we took |
|---|---|
| [Parsa013Ah/OpenCode-Unlimited-ProxyPool](https://github.com/Parsa013Ah/OpenCode-Unlimited-ProxyPool) | Personal + public proxy pool, disk cache, V2Ray-ready config layout, dashboard, Node/Express shape |
| [ebouther/opencode-unlimited-proxy](https://github.com/ebouther/opencode-unlimited-proxy) | Free-tier fingerprint gates (`stream: true`, tool named `read`), rotate-on-403/429, explicit “does not remove quota” stance |
| [Tazmyan/OpenCode-Unlimited](https://github.com/Tazmyan/OpenCode-Unlimited) | Identity / project-id rotation guidance, status CLI, proxy routing notes |
| [Netherstar44/OpenCode_Unlimited](https://github.com/Netherstar44/OpenCode_Unlimited) | Process hygiene & cache-reset guidance adapted for Linux/proot |

Designed for **Debian proot** (Termux, proot-distro, etc.): pure Node, no Docker, low memory.

> **ToS note.** Rotating egress or identity to multiply free-tier budget may violate OpenCode’s terms. This project does not claim affiliation with OpenCode / Anomaly. Use at your own risk.

---

## Quick start (Debian proot)

```bash
# Node 18+ required
cd opencode-unlimited
npm install
cp config/custom-proxies.example.txt config/custom-proxies.txt
# edit custom-proxies.txt with your SOCKS/HTTP proxies (strongly recommended)

npm start
```

- Dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:8787/
- OpenAI base URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`
- API key: any string (default `openAuth`)
- Health: `http://127.0.0.1:8787/health`

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/models
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer local" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}'
```

### Point OpenCode at the gateway

In `opencode.json` (project or global):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "unlimited": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "OpenCode Unlimited",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1",
        "apiKey": "local"
      },
      "models": {
        "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free": { "name": "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free" },
        "glm-5.3-flash-free": { "name": "GLM 5.3 Flash Free" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

(Exact provider schema may vary by OpenCode version; use `/models` or the live list from the gateway.)

---

## CLI

```bash
npx opencode-unlimited status      # config + OpenCode paths
npx opencode-unlimited health     # live gateway status
npx opencode-unlimited proxy add 'socks5://127.0.0.1:1080'
npx opencode-unlimited proxy list
npx opencode-unlimited id-hint    # identity rotation (Tazmyan-style)
npx opencode-unlimited reset-hint # process hygiene (Netherstar-style)
```

---

## Proxies

**Personal proxies are required for reliable free-tier access.** Public lists rarely survive OpenCode’s checks.

1. Copy `config/custom-proxies.example.txt` → `config/custom-proxies.txt`
2. Add one proxy per line (`socks5://…`, `http://…`, etc.)
3. Or set `PROXY_CUSTOM=socks5://…,http://…`

V2Ray share links / subscriptions: put them in `config/v2ray.txt` (layout ready; full Xray-core manager can be added later — current release focuses on classic HTTP/SOCKS + fingerprint + rotation).

---

## Environment

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8787` | Listen port |
| `BIND` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address |
| `PROXY_ENABLED` | `1` | Enable pool |
| `PROXY_CUSTOM` | — | Comma-separated personal proxies |
| `OPENCODE_UPSTREAM` | `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` | Primary upstream |

---

## What this does **not** do

- Does not remove upstream per-egress-block quotas (daily reset ~00:00 UTC).
- Does not ship Cloudflare WARP (ebouther’s Docker/WARP path needs privileged networking unsuitable for typical proot).
- Does not auto-edit OpenCode identity files (CLI only prints safe steps).

---

## License

MIT. Community-derived ideas; original implementation. Not affiliated with OpenCode, Anomaly, or the upstream authors of the referenced repos.

# OpenCode Local Gateway

A small, dependency-free OpenAI-compatible HTTP gateway for OpenCode v2 on Debian/proot. It forwards requests to **one configured provider endpoint**, keeps provider credentials out of OpenCode's config, streams responses, and passes upstream errors (including `429` and `Retry-After`) through unchanged. It does not rotate identities, proxies, or credentials, disguise requests, or bypass provider limits.

## Requirements

- Debian or Debian proot (Termux/proot-distro is fine)
- Node.js 18 or newer (`node --version`)
- An OpenAI-compatible API endpoint and credentials you are authorized to use

No Docker, native modules, or npm dependencies are required.

## Run

```sh
cd opencode-gateway
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env and set UPSTREAM_BASE_URL, UPSTREAM_API_KEY, and a unique GATEWAY_API_KEY.
set -a
. ./.env
set +a
npm start
```

The gateway listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default. Check it with:

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/health
```

The health endpoint reports the upstream origin only; it does not expose credentials. The gateway requires its local bearer key on `/v1/*` requests. Do not bind it to a public interface unless you have separately secured it.

## Configure OpenCode v2

Add a provider entry to your OpenCode config (commonly `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "local-gateway": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Local Gateway",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1",
        "apiKey": "replace-with-the-same-GATEWAY_API_KEY-from-.env"
      },
      "models": {
        "your-model-id": {
          "name": "Your provider model"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Replace `your-model-id` with a model your upstream account supports. Keep provider credentials in `.env`, not in the OpenCode config. The gateway forwards `/v1/*` requests and query strings to the configured base URL; it does not pick or invent model IDs.

## Debian/proot notes

- Install Node.js 18+ using a source appropriate for your Debian release; verify with `node --version`.
- Keep `BIND=127.0.0.1` for local use. A proot localhost listener is generally reachable by programs running in that same environment.
- Start the gateway in a persistent terminal or a process manager available in your environment. Stop it with `Ctrl-C`.
- If using another compatible provider, set `UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` to that provider's API base and configure any custom auth header/scheme it documents (`UPSTREAM_AUTH_HEADER`, `UPSTREAM_AUTH_SCHEME`).

## Behavior and safety

- No automatic retry on `403`, `429`, or other provider errors: the original status, body, and `Retry-After` header are passed back to the client.
- Uses a fixed upstream URL and the configured credentials; no public proxy lists, egress rotation, identity changes, or request fingerprint manipulation.
- Local bearer authentication is required. Never share `.env`; it contains secrets.
- The proxy accepts `GET` and `POST` under `/v1/`, limits request bodies to 64 MiB, and exposes `/health`.

## Test

```sh
npm test
```

# Skill: OpenCode

# OpenCode

Use this guide as the starting point for work involving OpenCode itself. It
covers the core concepts needed to configure and customize OpenCode, extend it
with plugins, and build integrations with the OpenCode SDK, clients, and API.

Full documentation is available at <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/>. This overview is
only an index of core concepts. Before answering a question about a topic below,
fetch the URL named in that section and use the full page as the source of
truth. Follow links from that page when the question needs more detail. Fetch
<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> first when you need to discover the relevant
documentation page.

A machine-readable documentation index is available at
<https://opencode.ai/v2/llms.txt>.

## Version policy

Always answer for OpenCode V2 unless the user explicitly asks about V1,
legacy OpenCode, or migrating from V1.

Use only <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> documentation as the source of truth for V2.
Do not use <https://opencode.ai/docs/>, which documents V1, and do not use
general web search to resolve a V2 documentation question when the V2 docs or
linked pages cover it. The schema served from
<https://opencode.ai/config.json> accepts both V2 fields and deprecated V1
fields. Never recommend a field it marks deprecated. If V2 documentation is
missing or contradictory, state the uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of falling back to V1.

V1 documentation and syntax may be consulted only when the user explicitly
asks about V1 or when needed as migration input. Outputs and recommendations
must still use V2 unless the user specifically requests a V1 result.

## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Config changes apply without a restart. OpenCode watches config files and
reloads agents, commands, skills, MCP servers, and plugins after a save. The TUI
does the same for `cli.json`. To force a full reload, use `/reload`. Don't tell
the user to restart OpenCode after editing config.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/www/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. Restart it only if it is stuck or unhealthy, not to apply
configuration changes:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

Use OpenCode's built-in `api` command for local requests. It uses the same
discovery and authentication flow as the TUI and may start the background
service when no compatible healthy service is available. It accepts either an
HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:

```sh
opencode api post /api/example --data '{"key":"value"}'
opencode api get /api/example --header 'X-Example:value'
```

Request bodies default to `Content-Type: application/json`. When OpenCode is
connected to an explicit server instead of its managed background service, use
the same configured server and authentication context rather than constructing
an unauthenticated request separately.

See the [full API reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api) for available
endpoints, parameters, request bodies, and response schemas. The
raw [OpenAPI specification](https://opencode.ai/v2/openapi.json) is also
available for code generation and other tooling.

## [Client](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client)

For questions about connecting an application to OpenCode over the network,
fetch the full [client guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client) before
answering.

`@opencode/client` is the generated TypeScript client for the OpenCode HTTP
API. Its methods and types come from the same contract as the API reference.
The default entrypoint exposes Promise-based resource clients and async
iterables for streaming endpoints. The `@opencode/client/effect` entrypoint
exposes typed Effects, Streams, and decoded OpenCode schema values. Its
`Service` API can discover, start, stop, and authenticate with the local
background service from a Node application.

## [SDK](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk)

For questions about embedding OpenCode directly in an application, fetch the
full [SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk) before answering. The SDK
hosts OpenCode in the application without opening an HTTP listener.

Use the [Effect SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/effect) for
Effect applications. For Cloudflare Durable Objects, use the
[Cloudflare SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/cloudflare).

## [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)

OpenCode runs a client and a background server. Start by determining whether a
problem belongs to the client, the shared server, or one project.

- Check the service with `opencode service status` and verify the API with
  `opencode api get /api/info`.
- Compare with `opencode --standalone`, which runs the TUI with a private
  server, to isolate shared-service issues.
- Inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. Filter `role=cli` for
  client startup and `role=server` for sessions, providers, plugins,
  permissions, and tools.
- Run one reproduction with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` when normal logs are not
  sufficient.
- Do not delete or edit the database, service registration, or service config
  while diagnosing a problem. Back up persistent data before inspecting it
  with external tools.
- Redact API keys, authorization headers, prompts, file contents, and other
  sensitive data before sharing diagnostics.

See the [full troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)
for service lifecycle commands, API inspection, log locations, explicit server
connections, issue-reporting details, and local development paths.

## Docker

Docker images use versioned tags, for example `ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:2.0.0`.

## Connect

OpenCode has built-in support for many LLM providers. You can connect to them
directly [in the TUI](/cli/providers) with `/connect`.

See [Providers](/providers) to configure custom providers.

If you'd like easy access to the best coding models, you can try out

---

## Customize

Make OpenCode your own by editing the [OpenCode config](/config), [loading plugins](/plugins), [connecting MCP
servers](/mcp-servers), or [creating commands](/commands). For terminal interface themes and keybindings, see [CLI
settings](/cli/config).

---

## Learn

If you are interested in an in-depth course on OpenCode, Boot.dev has created an excellent [AI Coding with
OpenCode](https://www.boot.dev/courses/learn-ai-coding) course in consultation with our team. All the information in the course is
free to read and watch, though some interactive features may require payment.

# Intro

Run the CLI in a project to open the full-screen terminal interface:

```bash
opencode
```

Pass a directory to work in a different project:

```bash
opencode ~/code/my-project
```

Suggested terminals:

- [Ghostty](https://ghostty.org)
- [WezTerm](https://wezterm.org)
- [Alacritty](https://alacritty.org)
- [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/)

Truecolor support gives themes their most accurate colors; terminals without it use an approximation of the available
palette.

## Automation

Use `opencode run` to submit a prompt without opening the interactive interface. It is designed for scripts, CI jobs, and
other workflows that need model output directly in the terminal.

```bash
opencode run "Explain this repository"
```

## Mini

Use `opencode mini` to start OpenCode's minimal interactive interface instead of the full-screen TUI.

```bash
opencode mini
```

Run `opencode mini --help` to see its session, model, agent, prompt, and replay options.

## Background service

By default, OpenCode discovers or starts one shared background server for your user account. Every local OpenCode client
connects to that server, which owns sessions, configuration, integrations, permissions, and tool execution.

Use `--standalone` to run with a private server, or `--server` to connect to a specific server URL:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$ROOT/opencode-gateway/.env"

if [[ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  echo "Missing $ENV_FILE. Copy opencode-gateway/.env.example to .env and add your API key." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# The .env file is a private, shell-compatible local configuration file.
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$ENV_FILE"
set +a

if [[ -z "${UPSTREAM_BASE_URL:-}" || -z "${UPSTREAM_API_KEY:-}" || "$UPSTREAM_API_KEY" == replace-* ]]; then
  echo "Set UPSTREAM_BASE_URL and a valid UPSTREAM_API_KEY in opencode-gateway/.env." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ -z "${GATEWAY_API_KEY:-}" || "$GATEWAY_API_KEY" == replace-* ]]; then
  echo "Set a unique GATEWAY_API_KEY in opencode-gateway/.env." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Node.js 18 or newer is required. Install it for Debian/proot, then rerun this script." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! node -e 'process.exit(Number(process.versions.node.split(".")[0]) >= 18 ? 0 : 1)' ; then
  echo "Node.js 18 or newer is required (found $(node --version))." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "OpenCode is not installed. Install it with: curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash" >&2
  exit 1
fi

export OPENCODE_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$GATEWAY_API_KEY"
GATEWAY_URL="http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-8787}"
GATEWAY_PID=""

health_check() {
  GATEWAY_URL="$GATEWAY_URL" node --input-type=module -e '
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`${process.env.GATEWAY_URL}/health`)
      const health = await response.json()
      process.exit(response.ok && health.ok === true ? 0 : 1)
    } catch {
      process.exit(1)
    }
  ' >/dev/null 2>&1
}

cleanup() {
  if [[ -n "$GATEWAY_PID" ]] && kill -0 "$GATEWAY_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$GATEWAY_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$GATEWAY_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

if ! health_check; then
  node "$ROOT/opencode-gateway/src/server.mjs" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  GATEWAY_PID=$!
  for _ in {1..30}; do
    if health_check; then
      break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 "$GATEWAY_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Gateway exited before becoming healthy. Check its configuration and port ${PORT:-8787}." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
fi

if ! health_check; then
  echo "Gateway did not become healthy at $GATEWAY_URL/health." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"
exec opencode --standalone "$@"

A small, quota-respecting OpenAI-compatible gateway for OpenCode v2 on Debian/proot. It forwards requests to one provider endpoint configured by you, streams responses, and preserves upstream errors and rate-limit responses. It does not claim to provide unlimited usage or bypass provider limits.

## Quick start

1. Install Node.js 18+ and OpenCode v2.
2. Copy `opencode-gateway/.env.example` to `opencode-gateway/.env` and set your valid upstream API key and a unique local gateway key.
3. Run `./start-opencode.sh` from the repository root.

This starts the local gateway and launches OpenCode with the ready-to-use v2 config in [`opencode.json`](opencode.json). Read [`opencode-gateway/README.md`](opencode-gateway/README.md) for configuration, supported models, and tests. The credentials in `.env` are local setup values; the included upstream key is only a placeholder, not a working credential.

The repository also contains `opencode-unlimited.zip`, an unmodified legacy archive unrelated to this setup. Do not run that archive.

1: # OpenCode Local Gateway
2: 
3: A small, dependency-free OpenAI-compatible HTTP gateway for OpenCode v2 on Debian/proot. It forwards requests to **one configured provider endpoint**, keeps provider credentials out of OpenCode's config, streams responses, and passes upstream errors (including `429` and `Retry-After`) through unchanged. It does not rotate identities, proxies, or credentials, disguise requests, or bypass provider limits.
4: 
5: ## Requirements
6: 
7: - Debian or Debian proot (Termux/proot-distro is fine)
8: - Node.js 18 or newer (`node --version`)
9: - An OpenAI-compatible API endpoint and credentials you are authorized to use
10: 
11: No Docker, native modules, or npm dependencies are required.
12: 
13: ## One-command Debian/proot startup
14: 
15: From the repository root, create and edit the private environment file once:
16: 
17: ```sh
18: cp opencode-gateway/.env.example opencode-gateway/.env
19: # Edit opencode-gateway/.env and set a valid UPSTREAM_API_KEY and a unique GATEWAY_API_KEY.
20: chmod +x start-opencode.sh
21: ```
22: 
23: Install Node.js 18+ and OpenCode v2 if they are not already installed. Then start the gateway and OpenCode together with:
24: 
25: ```sh
26: ./start-opencode.sh
27: ```
28: 
29: The launcher loads `opencode-gateway/.env`, starts the gateway if its health endpoint is not already available, exports the local gateway credential to OpenCode, and runs OpenCode in this repository using the included `opencode.json`. Any arguments are passed through to OpenCode. When the OpenCode process exits, a gateway started by the launcher is stopped. To run OpenCode against a different upstream model, change the selected model in `opencode.json` to one of the model IDs listed in its provider block (or edit that list to match models supported by your account).
30: 
31: The gateway listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default. Check it with:
32: 
33: ```sh
34: curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/health
35: ```
36: 
37: The health endpoint reports the upstream origin only; it does not expose credentials. The gateway requires its local bearer key on `/v1/*` requests. Do not bind it to a public interface unless you have separately secured it.
38: 
39: ## OpenCode v2 config
40: 
41: The ready-to-use repo config is [`../opencode.json`](../opencode.json). Its custom-provider entry uses the OpenCode v2 `providers` / `package` / `settings.baseURL` schema and gets the local bearer credential from `OPENCODE_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, which the launcher supplies from `GATEWAY_API_KEY`. The upstream API credential stays in `.env` and is never placed in the OpenCode config.
42: 
43: For a different compatible upstream, set `UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` to its API base and configure any custom auth header/scheme it documents (`UPSTREAM_AUTH_HEADER`, `UPSTREAM_AUTH_SCHEME`). Make sure model IDs in `opencode.json` match the upstream's supported model IDs.
44: 
45: ## Debian/proot notes
46: 
47: - Install Node.js 18+ using a source appropriate for your Debian release; verify with `node --version`.
48: - Keep `BIND=127.0.0.1` for local use. A proot localhost listener is generally reachable by programs running in that same environment.
49: - Start the gateway in a persistent terminal or a process manager available in your environment. Stop it with `Ctrl-C`.
50: - If using another compatible provider, set `UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` to that provider's API base and configure any custom auth header/scheme it documents (`UPSTREAM_AUTH_HEADER`, `UPSTREAM_AUTH_SCHEME`).
51: 
52: ## Behavior and safety
53: 
54: - No automatic retry on `403`, `429`, or other provider errors: the original status, body, and `Retry-After` header are passed back to the client.
55: - Uses a fixed upstream URL and the configured credentials; no public proxy lists, egress rotation, identity changes, or request fingerprint manipulation.
56: - Local bearer authentication is required. Never share `.env`; it contains secrets.
57: - The proxy accepts `GET` and `POST` under `/v1/`, limits request bodies to 64 MiB, and exposes `/health`.
58: 
59: ## Test
60:

62: npm test
63: ```

# OpenCode Local Gateway

A small, dependency-free OpenAI-compatible gateway for OpenCode v2 on Debian/proot. It lets you select either OpenRouter's free-model router or the Gemini API from one OpenCode provider config. Each request is sent only to the selected provider using that provider's own key and quota. Upstream errors (including `429` and `Retry-After`) pass through unchanged; there are no retries, key rotations, or limit bypasses.

## Requirements

- Debian or Debian proot (Termux/proot-distro is fine)
- Node.js 18 or newer (`node --version`)
- Your OpenRouter and/or Gemini API key

No Docker, native modules, or npm dependencies are required.

## One-command Debian/proot startup

From the repository root, create and edit the private environment file once:

```sh
cp opencode-gateway/.env.example opencode-gateway/.env
chmod 600 opencode-gateway/.env
# Edit opencode-gateway/.env and add at least one provider key plus a unique GATEWAY_API_KEY.
chmod +x start-opencode.sh
```

Install Node.js 18+ and OpenCode v2 if they are not already installed. Then start the gateway and OpenCode together with:

```sh
./start-opencode.sh
```

The launcher loads `opencode-gateway/.env`, starts the gateway if its health endpoint is not already available, exports the local gateway credential to OpenCode, and runs OpenCode in this repository using `opencode.json`. Any arguments are passed through to OpenCode. When OpenCode exits, a gateway started by the launcher is stopped.

The default model is `local-gateway/openrouter-free`. Select `local-gateway/gemini-flash` in OpenCode to use Gemini. You may set either provider key or both; models whose key is not configured will return a clear error. Both aliases can be pointed at another supported model by changing `OPENROUTER_MODEL` or `GEMINI_MODEL` in `.env`.

## Provider model IDs

- **OpenRouter:** The default upstream model is `openrouter/free`, OpenRouter's free-model router. It selects from eligible free models according to OpenRouter's current availability. To pin another model, set `OPENROUTER_MODEL` to its exact OpenRouter model ID.
- **Gemini:** The default upstream model is `gemini-3.8-flash` at Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. To use another model available to your API key, set `GEMINI_MODEL` to its exact model ID.

Free-tier model availability, rate limits, and quotas are determined by each provider and can change. If a provider reports a limit or unavailable model, wait or choose another model supported by your account; this setup does not circumvent those limits.

## Gateway details

The gateway listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default. Check it with:

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/health
```

The health endpoint reports configured provider names and origins only; it does not expose credentials. The gateway requires its local bearer key on `/v1/*` requests. Keep `BIND=127.0.0.1`; do not bind it to a public interface unless you have separately secured it.

The ready-to-use repo config is [`../opencode.json`](../opencode.json). Its custom-provider entry uses the OpenCode v2 `providers` / `package` / `settings.baseURL` schema and gets the local bearer credential from `OPENCODE_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, which the launcher supplies from `GATEWAY_API_KEY`. Upstream credentials remain in `.env` and are never placed in the OpenCode config.

## Behavior and safety

- No automatic retries on `403`, `429`, or other provider errors; status, response body, and `Retry-After` are passed through.
- Fixed provider endpoints and configured credentials; no public proxy lists, egress rotation, identity changes, or request fingerprint manipulation.
- Local bearer authentication is required. Never share `.env`; it contains secrets.
- The proxy accepts `GET` and `POST` under `/v1/`, limits request bodies to 64 MiB, and exposes `/health`.

## Test

```sh
cd opencode-gateway
npm test
```
